To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we developed a DNA-based vaccine that targets the Δ16HER-2 splice variant, which is the transforming isoform of HER-2 in HER2+ breast cancer.

(i) we identified the immunogenic epitopes in the Δ16HER 2 isoform of human HER2; (ii) we developed DNA vaccines that hamper breast carcinogenesis; and (iii) phage-based vaccines break the tolerogenic mechanisms against human HER2, eliciting a protective humoral response against breast cancer.
we identified structural and immunogenic differences in Δ16HER 2 and HER2 proteins and developed phage-based antiHER2/ΔHER2 vaccines to circumvent tolerance in HER2 positive breast cancer.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel anti-cancer therapies based on the use of DNA and phage vectors.
the identification and characterization of novel therapeutic targets and the development and validation of new therapeutic strategies to improve cancer treatment.
the development of new immunotherapeutic approaches against breast cancer, specifically HER2-positive breast tumors, which are the most aggressive type.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
phage-based antiHER2 vaccination can circumvent immune tolerance against HER2 breast cancer, allowing for improved anti-tumor responses.
phage-based vaccination against Δ16HER2 can break immune tolerance and induce an effective immune response against breast cancer.
the phage-based vaccines are a novel and promising approach that can be used in the treatment of patients with HER2-positive breast and other cancers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the HER2 protein is a self-antigen in HER2+ breast cancer patients.
we developed a DNA vaccine and a phage-based vaccine to target the Δ16HER-2 isoform.
we have developed a new vaccine strategy to break immune tolerance against HER2+ breast cancers.
The main takeaway from our work is that
phage-based anti-tumor vaccination is a promising strategy to break tolerance against HER2-positive cancer cells.
phage-based vaccines against HER2/Δ16 HER2 can break immune tolerance in HER2-positive tumors and induce a potent antitumor immune response.
phage-based vaccines against Δ16HER2 can be used as a safe and effective immunotherapy against HER 2-positive breast cancers.
